items.title: At Least 6 Dead in Poland After Gunman Opens Fire in Krakow, Police Say
items.summary: The authorities said that the gunman, who began shooting from a car near a market square, was shot and taken to a hospital.
items.full_text:
Title: At Least 6 Dead in Poland After Gunman Opens Fire in Krakow, Police Say - The New York Times

URL Source: https://www.nytimes.com/2026/11/07/world/europe/krakow-poland-shooting.html

Published Time: Sat, 07 Nov 2026 23:36:32 GMT

Markdown Content:
A gunman shot dead at least six people on Saturday in the medieval heart of the Polish city of Krakow, the authorities said, in an attack that struck at the height of the weekend rush in a popular market square.

Officials identified the gunman as a 24-year-old Polish citizen but did not give a name or possible motive for the shooting, which ended after the police wounded and apprehended the assailant.

The gunman, according to the police, began firing from a car he had driven into Krakow’s market square, a popular tourist destination in the city’s Old Town, at around 3 p.m.

Six people died and at least 15 more were wounded in the attack, said Krakow’s mayor, Lukasz Gibala. “Emergency services are currently at work. I ask for calm and responsibility,” he said in a statement. A police official later raised the number of people injured to 16, saying that five of them were foreigners.

Poland’s police chief, Marek Boron, said that a British citizen was among the two men and four women killed. Two of the dead, he said, have not yet been identified.

State news media reported that the gunman had been wounded in fire from police officers patrolling the area and taken to a hospital.

Poland’s interior minister, Marcin Kierwinski, said that the wounded included two police officers, one of whom was in “a very critical condition.” He suggested that the gunman was “fascinated by far-right ideologies” but did not give details.

Mass shootings are extremely rare in Poland, but the war in neighboring Ukraine has stirred alarm about an increase in the supply of weapons, which are tightly controlled.

Image

![Image 1: Emergency personnel in beige and neon yellow uniforms attend to a person in a blue jacket who is seated on a ledge on the street.](https://static01.nyt.com/images/2026/11/07/multimedia/07int-poland-shooting-fwjl/07int-poland-shooting-fwjl-articleLarge.jpg?quality=75&auto=avif&disable=upscale)

Emergency personnel tending to a person near Krakow’s main market square after a shooting in the Polish city on Saturday.Credit...Jakub Porzycki/Reuters

Prime Minister Donald Tusk, in a meeting with security officials in Krakow on Saturday evening, said that, based on drone footage of the gunman’s residence, “there are likely deceased people inside the perpetrator’s home.”

The gunman is not from Krakow but Ostrowiec Swietokrzyski, a town northeast of Krakow.

Previously, Mr. Tusk had posted a message on social media praising the “heroic police officers who acted at the risk of their own lives.” He added a plea to “politicians of all stripes: do not exploit this tragedy.”

Political tempers have risen sharply over the past week during [a volatile standoff at Poland’s Constitutional Tribunal in Warsaw](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/10/31/world/europe/poland-court-police-president.html), where newly appointed pro-government judges announced on Oct. 31 that they had suspended the chief justice, an ally of the previous governing party, Law and Justice. Riot police have surrounded the court for the past week, holding back right-wing protesters gathered outside.

Mr. Tusk’s right-wing opponents have accused Mr. Tusk of engineering a “coup d’état,” while the prime minister has insisted he only wants to end the capture of the court by judges appointed by Law and Justice, a right-wing nationalist party.

Poland’s president, Karol Nawrocki, an ally of Law and Justice who has led a chorus of accusations against Mr. Tusk, said on [social media](https://x.com/NawrockiKn/status/2119093125842862492?a=v4C-ZW5U5vDJ498LJK8&s=20) on Saturday that he expected a full investigation to determine the circumstances of the shooting, calling the public’s safety a priority.

Krakow’s sprawling market square, Rynek Glowny, forms the heart of the city’s medieval center and is dotted with cafes, music bars, restaurants, hotels and hostels, making it one of Poland’s most visited tourist destinations.

Callum Scott, 24, a British tourist in Krakow for the weekend, said he had just sat down at a restaurant in the square when the shooting began. “I thought it was fireworks, but the bangs just kept going and I saw people rushing toward us screaming in panic,” he said. He joined a crowd of people “sheltering shoulder to shoulder” in the lobby of a nearby hotel.

“The chaos,” he said, “was terrifying.”

Image

Police officers inspecting a car near Krakow’s main market square.Credit...Bartosz Siedlik/Agence France-Presse — Getty Images

Anatol Magdziarz contributed reporting from Warsaw.
